query: How do I unclog a bathroom sink drain without chemicals?
answer:
Start at the pop-up stopper, because that's where most bathroom sink clogs are: a wad of hair and soap scum caught on the stopper. Lift the stopper out. If it won't come up, loosen the nut on the pivot rod under the sink and pull the rod out first. Clean off the gunk, then fish around inside the drain with needle-nose pliers or a cheap plastic barbed drain strip, such as a Zip-It [1][2].

If water still drains slowly, take the stopper out and block the overflow hole with a wet rag. Then use a small cup plunger, which needs a good seal to work [1][2]. You can also try pouring in very hot water, or ½ cup of baking soda followed by 1 cup of vinegar. Let that sit for about 30 minutes, then flush it with hot water. This helps with minor buildup, but it won't break up a real hair clog [3].

If none of that works, put a bucket under the U-shaped P-trap and unscrew its slip nuts by hand or with pliers. Clean it out and put it back together, or run a small hand drain snake into the wall pipe [1][2]. One warning: if you already poured a chemical drain cleaner in and it didn't work, don't plunge or open the trap. It could splash caustic liquid on you, so call a plumber instead [2].
